9: ## About the name
10: 
11: The original name of this program was "C++check", but it was later changed to "Cppcheck".
12: 
13: Despite the name, Cppcheck is designed for both C and C++.
14: 
15: ## Manual
16: 
17: A manual is available [online](https://cppcheck.sourceforge.io/manual.pdf).
18: 
19: ## Donate CPU
20: 
21: Cppcheck is a hobby project with limited resources. You can help us by donating CPU (1 core, which is the default, or as many as you like. Use the `-j` flag to use more cores). It is simple:
22: 
23:  1. Download (and extract) Cppcheck source code.
24:  2. Run (Linux/MacOS example):
25: 
26:     ```shell
27:     cd cppcheck/
28:     python3 -m venv .venv
29:     source .venv/bin/activate
30: 
31:     pip install -r tools/donate-cpu-requirements.txt
32:     ./tools/donate-cpu.py
33:     ```
34: 
35: The script will analyse Debian source code and upload the results to a Cppcheck server. We need these results both to improve Cppcheck and to detect regressions.
36: 
37: You can stop the script whenever you like with Ctrl+C.
38: 
39: ## Compiling
40: 
41: Cppcheck requires a C++ compiler with (partial) C++11 support. Minimum required versions are GCC 5.1 / Clang 3.5 / AppleClang 6.0 / Visual Studio 2015.
42: 
43: To build the GUI application, you need to use the CMake build system.
44: 
45: When building the command line tool, [PCRE](http://www.pcre.org/) is optional. It is used if you build with rules.
46: 
47: There are multiple compilation choices:
48: 
49: * CMake - cross platform build tool
50: * (Windows) Visual Studio
51: * (Windows) Qt Creator + MinGW
52: * GNU compilers - via make or directly
53: 
54: The minimum required Python version is 3.7.
55: 
56: ### CMake
57: 
58: The minimum required version is CMake 3.22.
59: 
60: Example, compiling Cppcheck with cmake:
61: 
62: ```shell
63: cmake -S . -B build
64: cmake --build build
65: ```
66: 
67: If you want to compile the GUI you can use the flag.
68: `-DBUILD_GUI=ON`
69: 
70: For rules support (requires pcre) use the flag.
71: `-DHAVE_RULES=ON`
72: 
73: For release builds it is recommended that you use:
74: `-DUSE_MATCHCOMPILER=ON`
75: 
76: For building the tests use the flag.
77: `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`
78: 
79: Using CMake you can generate project files for Visual Studio, XCode, etc.
80: 
81: #### Building a specific configuration
82: 
83: For single-configuration generators (like "Unix Makefiles") you can generate and build a specific configuration (e.g. "`RelWithDebInfo`") using:
84: 
85: ```shell
86: cmake -S . -B build_RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo ..
87: cmake --build build_RelWithDebInfo --config RelWithDebInfo
88: ```
89: 
90: For multi-configuration generators (like "Visual Studio 17 2022") the same is achieved using:
91: 
92: ```shell
93: cmake -S . -B build
94: cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo
95: ```
96: 
97: ### Visual Studio
98: 
99: Use the `cppcheck.sln` file. The file is configured for Visual Studio 2019, but the platform toolset can be changed easily to older or newer versions. The solution contains platform targets for both x86 and x64.
100: 
101: To compile with rules, select "`Release-PCRE`" or "`Debug-PCRE`" configuration. `pcre.lib` (`pcre64.lib` for x64 builds) and `pcre.h` are expected to be in `/externals` then. A current version of PCRE for Visual Studio can be obtained using [vcpkg](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg).
102: 
103: ### Visual Studio (from command line)
104: 
105: If you do not wish to use the Visual Studio IDE, you can compile Cppcheck from the command line the following command.
106: 
107: ```shell
108: msbuild cppcheck.sln
109: ```
110: 
111: ### VS Code
112: 
113: Cppcheck Official is an extension officially supported by the cppcheck team allowing you to easily use cppcheck in VS Code. You can find it in VS Code Marketplace through the extension tab in your IDE. For instructions on how to set it up and use it, see the readme on the github page: <https://github.com/cppchecksolutions/vscode-cppcheck-official>
114: 
115: ### Qt Creator + MinGW
116: 
117: The PCRE dll is needed to build the CLI. It can be downloaded here:
118: <http://software-download.name/pcre-library-windows/>
119: 
120: ### GNU compilers
121: 
122: #### GNU make
123: 
124: Simple, unoptimized build (no dependencies):
125: 
126: ```shell
127: make
128: ```
129: 
130: You can use `CXXOPTS`, `CPPOPTS` and `LDOPTS` to append to the existing `CXXFLAGS`, `CPPFLAGS` and `LDFLAGS` instead of overriding them.
131: 
132: The recommended release build is:
133: 
134: ```shell
135: make MATCHCOMPILER=yes FILESDIR=/usr/share/cppcheck HAVE_RULES=yes CXXOPTS="-O2" CPPOPTS="-DNDEBUG"
136: ```
137: 
138: #### g++ (for experts)
139: 
140: If you just want to build Cppcheck without dependencies then you can use this command:
141: 
142: ```shell
143: g++ -o cppcheck -std=c++11 -Iexternals -Iexternals/simplecpp -Iexternals/tinyxml2 -Iexternals/picojson -Ilib -Ifrontend frontend/*.cpp cli/*.cpp lib/*.cpp externals/simplecpp/simplecpp.cpp externals/tinyxml2/tinyxml2.cpp
144: ```
145: 
146: #### Flags
147: 
148: * `MATCHCOMPILER=yes`
149:    Several `Token` matching patterns are converted into more efficient C++ code at compile time (requires Python to be installed).
150: 
151: * `FILESDIR=/usr/share/cppcheck`
152:    Specifies the folder where Cppcheck files (addons, cfg, platform) are installed to.
153: 
154: * `HAVE_RULES=yes`
155:    Enables rules (requires PCRE to be installed).
156: 
157: * `CXXOPTS="-O2"`
158:    Enables most compiler optimizations.
159: 
160: * `CPPOPTS="-DNDEBUG"`
161:    Disables assertions.
162: 
163: * `HAVE_BOOST=yes`
164:    Enables usage of more efficient container from Boost (requires Boost to be installed).
165: 
166: ### MinGW
167: 
168: ```shell
169: mingw32-make
170: ```
171: 
172: If you encounter the following error with `MATCHCOMPILER=yes` you need to specify your Python interpreter via `PYTHON_INTERPRETER`.
173: 
174: ```text
175: process_begin: CreateProcess(NULL, which python3, ...) failed.
176: makefile:24: pipe: No error
177: process_begin: CreateProcess(NULL, which python, ...) failed.
178: makefile:27: pipe: No error
179: makefile:30: *** Did not find a Python interpreter.  Stop.
180: ```
181: 
182: ### Other compiler/IDE
183: 
184: 1. Create an empty project file / makefile.
185: 2. Add all cpp files in the Cppcheck cli and lib folders to the project file / makefile.
186: 3. Add all cpp files in the externals folders to the project file / makefile.
187: 4. Compile.
188: 
189: ### Cross compiling Win32 (CLI) version of Cppcheck in Linux
190: 
191: ```shell
192: sudo apt-get install mingw32
193: make CXX=i586-mingw32msvc-g++ LDFLAGS="-lshlwapi" RDYNAMIC=""
194: mv cppcheck cppcheck.exe
195: ```
196: 
197: ## Packages
198: 
199: Besides building yourself on the platform of your choice there are also several ways to obtain pre-built packages.
200: 
201: ### Official
202: 
203: Official packages are maintained by the Cppcheck team.
204: 
205: * (Windows) An official Windows installer is available via the official Cppcheck SourceForge page: <https://cppcheck.sourceforge.io>.
206: * (Windows) Official builds of the current development versions are available via the [release-windows](https://github.com/cppcheck-opensource/cppcheck/actions/workflows/release-windows.yml) workflow. They are built nightly for the `main` branch and for each commit for release branches. As these are development versions please refrain from using these in production environments!
207:   * A portable package (i.e. does not require installation) is available as the `portable` artifact. This is still a work-in-progress - see <https://trac.cppcheck.net/ticket/10771> for details.
208:   * An installer is available via the `installer` artifact.
209: * (Multi-Platform) A premium version with additional features provided by the original author of Cppcheck is available for purchase via <https://www.cppcheck.com>.
210: 
211: ### Third-party
212: 
213: Third-party packages are ***not*** maintained by the Cppcheck team but their respective packagers.
214: 
215: *Note:* The following list is purely informational and listed in no particular order.
